assumptions.reason: Spec parameterizes HurstExponent(period=N) but never states N; chose 100 5-minute bars (~8.3 trading hours) as a reasonable single-window R/S lookback for intraday mean-reversion, long enough for a stable estimate while still short enough to warm up early in the 4680-bar series.

assumptions.choice: Single-window classic R/S: demean the window, cumulative-sum the deviations, R = max-min of that cumulative series, S = population standard deviation of the window, H = ln(R/S) / ln(N).
assumptions.reason: Spec explicitly names 'classic R/S rescaled range' and asks for the Hurst value 'over the last N bars' (one value per bar), so the textbook single-window formulation was used rather than a multi-scale log-log regression across several window sizes.

assumptions.choice: If S==0 or R==0 (flat price window), set Hurst=0.5.
assumptions.reason: log(R/S) is undefined when R or S is zero; 0.5 is the 'no memory' neutral value, keeping the indicator numerically defined without adding a filter the spec doesn't mention.

assumptions.choice: A standalone bt.Order.Stop sell/buy order is submitted from notify_order once the entry order fills, sized to match the filled entry, and is canceled if a signal exit fires first.
assumptions.reason: Spec says 'using stop orders or bracket orders' without specifying which; a standalone Stop order composes cleanly with the signal-based exits and the required order-tracking guard, rather than the coupled buy_bracket/sell_bracket helper.

assumptions.choice: Signals are evaluated in next() using the bar's close values; resulting orders fill at the next bar's open per backtrader's default.
assumptions.reason: Spec says 'process signals on bar close'; this matches backtrader's default order-execution timing with no cheat-on-close override implied, so no extra execution-timing configuration was added.
